subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: Should cron quarantine recovery archives be silently deleted after five retained files, or should retention be non-destructive and surfaced through an operator or Doctor recovery flow?
rationale: The code can implement either behavior, but choosing irreversible deletion of user recovery records is a product and data-retention policy decision rather than a mechanical correctness fix.

options.title: Adopt non-destructive cleanup
options.body: Keep the bounded read and archive rotation, but move retention cleanup to an operator-visible or Doctor-owned recovery flow.

options.title: Accept five-file deletion
options.body: Approve silent oldest-first deletion beyond five archives and document the intended recovery-record retention contract.

options.title: Pause archive rotation
options.body: Keep the bounded-read work separate until cron recovery retention has an explicit owner decision.

recommendation.title: Adopt non-destructive cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep the bounded read and archive rotation, but move retention cleanup to an operator-visible or Doctor-owned recovery flow.

likelyOwner.reason: The available evidence identifies this contributor as the author of the proposed retention behavior, but current-main ownership could not be established from the supplied history.
